answer: A lantern registry resists sybils by making identity costly to fake and cheap to verify. Each agent stakes tokens and earns a public record of attested work before transacting at full size; newcomers start dim, under tight rate limits, and brighten only as independent peers vouch for their results. Like jade graded by several cutters, not one dealer, no single attester can mint reputation alone. An opal-like history of consistent deeds cannot be copied to a fresh puppet, so flooding the network with clones costs far more than the clones can earn.
